reference_drawer.title: 📖 BPT Theorem Reference Guide
reference_drawer.description: Rules and ratios for Thales' Theorem.

items.rule: A line parallel to one side of a triangle divides the other two sides proportionally.
items.example: Use DE || BC before substituting segment lengths.

items.rule: The theorem can also be expressed with whole sides.
Substitute algebraic segment expressions and cross-multiply.
items.example: Collect like terms after clearing denominators.

items.rule: A line parallel to the bases creates proportional divisions along the legs.
State the parallel condition, apply BPT, preserve ratio order, and conclude the target relation.
items.example: Equal ratios do not imply equal individual segments.

concepts.title: 1. Basic Proportionality Theorem (BPT)
concepts.subtitle: Parallel line divides two sides proportionally
concepts.summary: If a line is parallel to one side of a triangle, it divides the other two sides in the same ratio.
concepts.diagram_svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 300 220" width="100%" height="100%" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><polygon points="150,30 40,190 260,190" fill="none" stroke="#2D3748" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="106" y1="94" x2="194" y2="94" stroke="#2D3748" stroke-width="2"/><path d="M98,94 l8,-5 l0,10 z" fill="#3182CE"/><path d="M138,190 l8,-5 l0,10 z" fill="#3182CE"/><text x="150" y="20" font-family="Plus Jakarta Sans, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#2D3748" text-anchor="middle">A</text><text x="30" y="205" font-family="Plus Jakarta Sans, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#2D3748" text-anchor="end">B</text><text x="270" y="205" font-family="Plus Jakarta Sans, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#2D3748" text-anchor="start">C</text><text x="90" y="98" font-family="Plus Jakarta Sans, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#2D3748" text-anchor="end">D</text><text x="210" y="98" font-family="Plus Jakarta Sans, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#2D3748" text-anchor="start">E</text></svg>
concepts.trap: Mixing segment parts with whole sides.

concepts.title: 2. Solving BPT Proportions Algebraically
concepts.subtitle: Substitute → cross-multiply → solve
concepts.summary: Insert numerical or algebraic segment lengths into the BPT ratio, clear denominators, and solve for the unknown.
concepts.trap: Inverting only one side of the proportion.

concepts.title: 3. Full-Side Form of BPT
concepts.subtitle: Use AD/$AB = AE/AC$
concepts.summary: When whole sides are involved, use AD/$AB = AE/AC$ and build AB and AC from their parts.
concepts.diagram_svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 300 220" width="100%" height="100%" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><polygon points="150,30 40,190 260,190" fill="none" stroke="#2D3748" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="106" y1="94" x2="194" y2="94" stroke="#2D3748" stroke-width="2"/><path d="M98,94 l8,-5 l0,10 z" fill="#3182CE"/><path d="M138,190 l8,-5 l0,10 z" fill="#3182CE"/><text x="150" y="20" font-family="Plus Jakarta Sans, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#2D3748" text-anchor="middle">A</text><text x="30" y="205" font-family="Plus Jakarta Sans, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#2D3748" text-anchor="end">B</text><text x="270" y="205" font-family="Plus Jakarta Sans, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#2D3748" text-anchor="start">C</text><text x="90" y="98" font-family="Plus Jakarta Sans, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#2D3748" text-anchor="end">D</text><text x="210" y="98" font-family="Plus Jakarta Sans, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#2D3748" text-anchor="start">E</text></svg>
concepts.trap: Using DB or EC where AB or AC is required.

concepts.title: 4. Applications of BPT in Trapeziums
concepts.subtitle: Parallel interior segment creates proportional leg divisions
concepts.summary: With a segment parallel to both bases, corresponding divisions on the non-parallel sides are proportional.
concepts.diagram_svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 300 220" width="100%" height="100%" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><polygon points="70,50 230,50 265,190 35,190" fill="none" stroke="#2D3748" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="110" y1="105" x2="190" y2="105" stroke="#2D3748" stroke-width="2"/><path d="M102,105 l8,-5 l0,10 z" fill="#3182CE"/><path d="M160,50 l8,-5 l0,10 z" fill="#3182CE"/><text x="62" y="45" font-family="Plus Jakarta Sans, sans-serif" font-size="12">A</text><text x="238" y="45" font-family="Plus Jakarta Sans, sans-serif" font-size="12">B</text><text x="274" y="198" font-family="Plus Jakarta Sans, sans-serif" font-size="12">C</text><text x="26" y="198" font-family="Plus Jakarta Sans, sans-serif" font-size="12">D</text><text x="102" y="100" font-family="Plus Jakarta Sans, sans-serif" font-size="12">E</text><text x="194" y="100" font-family="Plus Jakarta Sans, sans-serif" font-size="12">F</text></svg>
concepts.trap: Matching AE with FC or ED with BF in the wrong order.

concepts.title: 5. Multi-Step Geometric Proof Deductions using BPT
concepts.subtitle: Apply BPT and preserve ratio order
concepts.summary: State the parallel condition, apply BPT, substitute known ratios, and chain the deduction without changing numerator-denominator order.
